title: There is and want to
matching: Typed answers ignore letter case, extra spaces, apostrophe style and final . ! or ? punctuation. Accents and every other character count. Multiple-choice answers must match exactly.

lessons.title: There is and there are
lessons.explanation: Use there is to say that one thing exists or to describe a non-count noun, and there are for plural nouns: There is a book on the table. There is some milk. There are two chairs in the room. Questions put the verb first: Is there a bank near here? Are there any chairs? Short answers: Yes, there is. No, there aren't. Negatives: There isn't any milk. There aren't any chairs.

lessons.title: Want to + infinitive
lessons.explanation: Use want to plus the base verb to say what you wish to do: I want to learn English. She wants to go home. Add -s to want after he, she and it. Questions and negatives use do or does: Do you want to play tennis? She doesn't want to stay. After doesn't and don't the verb want has no -s. Do not leave out to, and do not use -ing: not I want learn or I want to learning.
